newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber weaker at close despite inquiries.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber weaker at close despite inquiries.

text.p: The Malaysian rubber market was weaker at the close despite some local dealers' covering and an Asian inquiry, dealers said.

"The market was weak because of Tokyo's falls. South Korea made inquiries for SMR 20 and is trying to buy at around 259 to 260 (cents a kg)," a dealer said. Suppliers were offering at around 262 cents.
"Otherwise there were basically no demand from other Asian buyers," he said. At the current levels, there were some covering by the European dealers ahead of the approaching summer holidays.
A dealer said raw material supply was sufficient to meet consumer demand. "Producers are also willing to sell for fear of falling prices," a trader said.
In earlier trading, some tonnages of SMR20 to Dubai were reported at 260 cents for June shipment.
A check with trading houses at noon showed the SMR 20 was offered at 262 cents, SMR CV at 332, SMR L at 308, SMR 10 at 263 and drum latex at 227.
At the close, July RSS1 buyer was down half cent at 284 cents ($1.12) a kg and July SMR 20 buyer eased 3.50 cents to 264.
The INRO five-day moving average was 216.29 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on June 4 against 215.90 on June 3. The daily indicator price was 216.76 against 216.78.
A Malaysian-based shipping agent quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $800 per TEU and $1,700 per two-TEU containers.
